title: How Adam Robinson tried to grow a bootstrapped SaaS like a VC-backed company, and what broke
summary: Adam Robinson recounts scaling retention.com to $21M ARR, then trying to build a unicorn in a year after watching Jasper's rise, missing targets on churn, competition and spending discipline. He also explains why LinkedIn founder content, free products, and stacking bootstrapped businesses are his core growth bets.

principles.text: Bootstrapping a profitable SaaS to ~$10-20M ARR lets you stack new ventures with fat free cash flow and freedom.
principles.quote: there is a point that you reach as a bootstrapper I don't know where it is maybe it's like 10 15 maybe 20 million AR if you've run it properly where it's so profitable

principles.text: Churn depends on product category; a system of record churns far less than a lead-gen tool, so don't assume a segment shift fixes churn.
principles.quote: if you're a CRM if you're a system of record that is the lowest churn product there is

principles.text: Being loud about early success invites competitors who undercut you at renewal, turning expansion into contraction.
principles.quote: all of a sudden we got five comp competitors and then renewals come around and the competitors are just like using builtwith hitting everybody up

principles.text: Bootstrappers who copy VC-style spending lose fiscal discipline; hiring 50 people in 60 days without processes failed.
principles.quote: I was just spending like a sailor setting a poor example everybody who worked for us spending like a sailor hiring super expensive employees

principles.text: Founder-led LinkedIn content, honest and in video, builds parasocial trust and is the most capital-efficient channel when buyers live there.
principles.quote: there could not possibly be a more Capital efficient way to spread awareness in in your buyers

principles.text: When stuck, the fix is a better product, not copying tactics; nothing works with a weak product.
principles.quote: everything works when your product is not good nothing works right so like the art of getting unstuck is the art of making everything that you're doing better
